_readme: Acknowledgements for the ADVISORY findings of scripts/check-build.py, and nothing else.
That script has two kinds of result. A hard failure (exit 1) stops a publish and
cannot be acknowledged here or anywhere: fix it. An advisory (exit 2) is something
true about the data that only a person can settle: two rips sharing a pack number, a
bare "Rochester", a product listed as upcoming that another file says is out.
An advisory that somebody has SEEN and that is waiting on an answer goes in
`acknowledged`. From then on the script still prints it, under 'already
acknowledged', and it no longer changes the exit code, so the nightly log is not
the same nineteen lines every night with a new one lost among them.
check   the tag in square brackets at the start of the finding: packs, rochester,
dash, upcoming, stale
match   text the finding must contain. Make it specific: for a pack finding it is
the series and the video ids, so a NEW rip joining the series changes the
finding and it comes back as unacknowledged.
date    the day it was acknowledged
why     who is being waited on, or why it is right as it stands
DELETE AN ENTRY WHEN ITS QUESTION IS ANSWERED. The script names any entry that no
longer matches anything, so this file cannot fill up with dead answers.
Every entry dated 2026-11-11 was written the night the checks went in, from the
findings they produced on the tree as it stood. None of them was a judgement that
the finding is wrong.

acknowledged.why: Not our sentence: these are the names of Wikimedia Commons categories, listed where the Garbage Plate page records which searches were run. The owner's rule exempts Commons filenames and categories by name.

A heading on the Garbage Plate page built on the inside/outside contrast, which the owner's rule names as an exception (qualifying it reads 'Outside Rochester, NY' as a place). Reported to the lead 11 November 2026 in case he wants it reworded anyway.
